summary.text: A rogue wave is an open-water wave much larger than the waves around it, with a height more than twice the significant wave height.
They can form when currents or winds make waves travel at different speeds and merge, or when energy shifts between waves to build one huge wave.
Once considered mythical, they are now proven to exist, and instruments recorded the 25.6 m Draupner wave in the North Sea in 1995.

facts.label: NOAA catalog, 2007
facts.value: Over 50 historical incidents probably linked to rogue waves

items.prompt: On a stretch of sea, the significant wave height is 5 m. Which single wave would oceanographers class as rogue?

options.label: A 6 m wave
An 8 m wave
An 11 m wave
A 9 m wave

items.explain: A rogue wave must be more than twice the significant wave height, so here it must top 10 m. Only the 11 m wave qualifies.

items.prompt: When the 2004 Asian tsunami struck, where were the only ships it sank?

options.label: Far out over deep ocean water
Tied up in port
Crossing mid-ocean shipping lanes
Anchored above deep sea trenches

items.explain: Tsunamis are nearly unnoticeable in deep water and only become dangerous near shore, so they do not threaten ships at sea. Rogue waves, by contrast, strike out at sea.

items.prompt: Before the 20th century, why were there so few firsthand reports of 30 m waves at sea?

options.label: Such waves form only in polar waters
Ships of the time stayed close to land
Sailors were forbidden to log the weather
Few people who met one lived to tell it

items.explain: Until steel double-hulled ships of the 20th century, people who met waves that size generally did not come back to describe them, which fed the disbelief.

items.prompt: Why can a rogue wave overwhelm a well-built ocean-going ship?

options.label: It goes far beyond what ship designers expect
It always hits the ship from directly below
It carries rocks and debris from the seabed
It arrives only at night, when crews are asleep

items.explain: Rogue waves can form suddenly and reach sizes far beyond the usual expectations of ship designers, so vessels not built for them can be overwhelmed.

items.prompt: In one proposed mechanism, an ordinary-looking wave suddenly grows huge for a short time. Where does its extra size come from?

options.label: An undersea quake lifts the water
The seabed rises sharply beneath it
It draws energy from nearby waves
It bounces back off a distant coast

items.explain: Through modulational instability, a normal wave can draw energy from other nearby waves and briefly become very large.

items.prompt: In 1995 a downward-pointing laser on the Draupner platform recorded a huge wave. What convinced people the reading was real and not a sensor fault?

options.label: A passing ship filmed the very same wave
Parts of the platform high above sea level were damaged
A satellite photographed the wave from orbit
Divers found the seabed scoured under the platform

items.explain: Minor damage appeared on the platform far above sea level, which confirmed the accuracy of the laser's wave-height reading.
